    AI Overview
    April 20 is widely recognized as a counterculture holiday for cannabis consumption (4/20) and is also celebrated as UN Chinese Language Day. It frequently falls within Volunteer Recognition Week and features observances like National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day and Lima Bean Respect Day. Historically, this date marks significant events, including the 1999 Columbine High School shooting. 
    Key Aspects of April 20: 
    • 4/20 Cannabis Culture: April 20 (4/20) is an unofficial holiday celebrating cannabis. It originated from a 1971 ritual among San Rafael High School students in California, who would meet at 4:20 p.m. to consume cannabis, note sources.
    • UN Chinese Language Day
      :
      Celebrated annually on April 20 to honor Cangjie, the legendary inventor of Chinese characters, and to promote cultural diversity.
    • Holidays & Observances:
      • Volunteer Recognition Day.
      • National Cheddar Fries Day.
      • National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day.
      • Look Alike Day.
    • Historical Events on April 20:
      • 1777: New York adopted its first state constitution.
      • 1940: RCA demonstrated the first electron microscope.
      • 1961: First rocket belt flight (Harold Graham).
      • 1999: The Columbine High School shooting.
      • 2008: Danica Patrick became the first woman to win an IndyCar race.
    • Birthdays on April 20: Notable birthdays often cited on this day include singer Luther Vandross and actor Shemar Moore. 
    Astrological Significance: 
    • April 20 marks the transition into the Taurus zodiac sign, frequently associated with a shift toward groundedness and a need for stability.

    AI Overview
    April 20th is most famously known as 420 Day, an unofficial global holiday for cannabis culture and advocacy. It is also recognized as UN Chinese Language Day, National Look-Alike Day, and National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day. The day is widely celebrated with gatherings and festivals focused on cannabis legalization. 
    Key Facts About April 20th: 
    • 4/20 Origin: While myths suggest it was a police code, the term 420 originated in the 1970s with a group of California high school students (the "Waldos") who met at 4:20 PM to smoke cannabis, a tradition later popularized by the band Grateful Dead.
    • Alternative Celebrations:
      • UN Chinese Language Day: Celebrated annually to honor Cangjie, the creator of Chinese characters.
      • National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day: A food holiday celebrating this specific dessert.
      • National Look-Alike Day: A day to celebrate people who look similar to others.
    • Other Days: National Lima Bean Respect Day, National Cheddar Fries Day, and Volunteer Recognition Day. 
    April 20th has become a significant day for activism to legalize marijuana for medical and recreational uses across the United States.

      AI Overview
      Notable events on April 20 include the 1999 Columbine High School massacre, the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil rig explosion, and the 1914 Ludlow Massacre in Colorado. Additionally, this date marks the 1967 bombing of Haiphong during the Vietnam War, and the 1940 demonstration of the first electron microscope. 
      Key Historical Events
      • 1861: Robert E. Lee resigned his commission in the United States Army. 
      • 1902: Pierre and Marie Curie refined radium chloride. 
      • 1912: Fenway Park in Boston and Tiger Stadium in Detroit opened for the first time. 
      • 1914: The Ludlow Massacre took place, where 19 men, women, and children were killed during a miners' strike. 
      • 1940: The first electron microscope was demonstrated. 
      • 1945: Soviet troops began their attack on Berlin. 
      • 1946: The League of Nations officially dissolved. 
      • 1971: The U.S. Supreme Court upheld the use of busing to desegregate schools. 
      • 1999: Two students committed a mass shooting at Columbine High School in Colorado, killing 13 people. 
      • 2010: The Deepwater Horizon oil rig exploded in the Gulf of Mexico, killing 11 workers and causing a massive oil spill. 
      Births and Cultural Notes 
      • 1889: Adolf Hitler was born.
      • 1893: Spanish painter Joan Miró was born.
      • 1949: Actress Jessica Lange was born.
      • 1964: Nutella appeared on store shelves for the first time.
      • 420 Day: April 20 is celebrated annually as a counterculture holiday for cannabis consumption and legalization advocacy.

        AI Overview
        On April 20, the most recognized unofficial holiday is 4/20, a celebration of cannabis culture. Other observed holidays include National Lima Bean Respect Day, National Cheddar Fries Day, National Look Alike Day, National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day, and Volunteer Recognition Day. 
        Key Holidays and Observances on April 20:
        • 420 Day (Weed Day): The unofficial marijuana culture holiday. 
        • National Lima Bean Respect Day: A day to recognize the nutrient-dense legume. 
        • National Cheddar Fries Day: Celebrating the popular appetizer. 
        • National Look Alike Day: A fun day often observed to recognize people who look similar. 
        • National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day: A day dedicated to the classic dessert. 
        • Volunteer Recognition Day: A day to thank volunteers for their service. 
        • UN Chinese Language Day: Celebrated to promote cultural exchange and multilingualism. 
        • National Death Doula Day: Observed to recognize the work of death doulas. 
        2026 Specific Observances (Monday, April 20): 
        • Patriots' Day: Often observed on the third Monday in April in Massachusetts and Maine.
        • Boston Marathon: Traditionally held on Patriots' Day.
        Cultural Significance of 4/20:
        Originating in the 1970s with a group of California students known as "the Waldos," the term "420" became a coded reference for searching for and consuming cannabis, now celebrated annually on April 20.

          AI Overview
          People born on April 20 typically fall under the zodiac sign Taurus (the Bull), which covers April 20 to May 20. As an earth sign ruled by Venus, they are often described as dependable, patient, and lovers of beauty. While often considered the start of Taurus, some traditions place this date on the cusp of Aries. 
          Usage Examples & Synonyms
          • Usage: A person born on this day might be described as a "Taurus," "April 20th Taurus," or, due to the transitional date, someone born on the "Aries-Taurus Cusp". 
          • Synonyms: Taurus is often referred to as "The Bull" or "The Lovers". 
          • Traits: Common descriptors include dependable, tenacious, earthy, and artistic. 
          Key Characteristics 
          • Element: Earth.
          • Ruling Planet: Venus.
          • Symbol: The Bull (♉).
          Note: In some astrological contexts, the sun transits Aries until the very end of April 19 or early April 20, making those born early on the 20th feel a blend of Aries energy, but officially it is the start of Taurus season.

            Scientific Discoveries. What are some scientific discoveries on April 20?
            About this result
            Feedback

            AI Overview
            Significant scientific milestones on April 20 include Marie and Pierre Curie isolating radioactive radium salts in 1902, the first pasteurization test by Louis Pasteur in 1862, and NASA selecting the Apollo 16 landing site in 1971. Furthermore, the Gravity Probe B satellite was launched in 2004 to confirm Einstein's relativity theories. 
            • 1902 - Isolation of Radium:
              Marie and Pierre Curie successfully isolated radioactive radium salts from pitchblende in Paris, a crucial step in the study of radioactivity. 
            • 1862 - First Pasteurization Test:
              Louis Pasteur and Claude Bernard completed the first successful test of pasteurization, a method to stop bacterial contamination in food and drink. 
            • 1972 - First Moon Telescope:
              Astronauts on the Apollo 16 mission landed on the Moon, setting up the first astronomical telescope on another planetary body (the FAR ultraviolet camera/spectrograph). 
            • 2004 - Gravity Probe B Launch:
              NASA launched the Gravity Probe B mission to test Albert Einstein's general theory of relativity, specifically the geodetic effect and frame-dragging. 
            • 1971 - Apollo 16 Landing Site Selection:
              NASA announced the selection of the Descartes Highlands for the Apollo 16 lunar landing. 
            Note: The results are based on historical records up to April 20, 2026.
